Rashi on Yevamot 31b:10:1.hebrew: לינחיה גבי עדים - מאי מהני? אי דכירי אימת הוה קידושין, אפי' אינו כתוב בשטר מצו לאסהודי. אלא להכי אמרת דמהני, דזימנין דלא דכירי וחזו מכתבא ואתו ומסהדי — והאי לאו עדות הוא, דרחמנא אמר: ע"פ שנים עדים (דברים י״ט:ט״ו), ולא שיעידו על פי כתבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:10:1.english: Let us leave it with the witnesses - What does [this] avail? If they remember when the betrothal took place, even if it is not written in the document, they are able to testify. Rather, you say that it avails for this [reason]: because sometimes they do not remember, and they see [it] from the writing and come and testify — and this is not [valid] testimony, for the Merciful One said: "By the mouth of two witnesses" (Deuteronomy 19:15), and not that they should testify from their writing.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:11:1.hebrew: גבי גירושין נמי - אמאי תקנו זמן? משום בת אחותו, גבי מאן נינחיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:11:1.english: Regarding divorce as well - [let us ask:] why did they institute [writing] a date? Because of his sister's daughter — [so] with whom should we leave it?

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:11:2.hebrew: להצלה דידה קאתי - וליכא למיחש דלמא מחקה ליה, דכי אתו סהדי דזינתה, אי לא מייתא שטרא דאיגרשה מקמי הכי, מוקמינן לה בחזקת אשת איש. ומיהו, אי לא תקון רבנן זמן, הוה מצי לאחפויי עלה, ומספיקא לא קטלינן לה; אבל השתא דתקון רבנן, אי לא מייתא ליה, מוקמינן לה אחזקה וקטלינן לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:11:2.english: It comes to save her - And there is no [reason] to be concerned lest she erase it, for when witnesses come [and testify] that she committed adultery, if she does not bring a document [proving] that she was divorced prior to that, we establish her in [her] presumptive status of a married woman. However, if the Rabbis had not instituted [writing] a date, [one] could cover up for her, and out of doubt we would not execute her; but now that the Rabbis instituted [it], if she does not bring it, we establish her upon [her] presumptive status and execute her.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:11:3.hebrew: הכא לחובה דידה קאתי - זמן דקידושין. ואי תקון לה רבנן זמן וזינתה, כבשה ליה לשטרא או מחקה ליה, וקיימא אחזקת פנויה כדמעיקרא:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:11:3.english: Here it comes to her disadvantage - [That is,] the date of betrothal. And if the Rabbis instituted a date for her, and she committed adultery, she would conceal the document or erase it, and remain in the presumptive status of an unmarried woman as before.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:13:1.hebrew: זיקת שני יבמין - דכל זמן שלא כנסה זה, עדיין זיקת ראשון עליה ונתוספת עליה זיקת מאמרו; הרי כשמת זה, נותרו עלה זיקת שניהם. ואילו כנסה, הוה פקעה זיקה דקמא, וכי מיית לא הוה עלה אלא זיקת שני. א"נ לא עבד בה מאמר, לא הוה עלה אלא זיקת ראשון:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:13:1.english: The levirate bond of two brothers-in-law - For as long as this [second brother] has not consummated the marriage with her, the levirate bond of the first [brother] is still upon her, and the bond of his ma'amar [levirate betrothal] is added upon her; thus, when this one died, the levirate bond of both of them remained upon her. Whereas if he had consummated the marriage with her, the bond of the first would have been dissolved, and when he died, only the bond of the second would have been upon her. Or alternatively, [if] he had not performed ma'amar with her, only the bond of the first would have been upon her.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:13:2.hebrew: מייבם לאיזו שירצה - כדקתני טעמא בפרק שני בברייתא: אם מאמרו של שני מאמר, אשת שני הוא בועל; ואם אינו מאמר, אשת ראשון הוא בועל:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:13:2.english: He may consummate the levirate marriage with whichever [woman] he wishes - As [the Gemara] teaches the reason in the second chapter in a baraita: If the levirate betrothal of the second [brother] is a [valid] levirate betrothal, it is the wife of the second [brother] with whom he has intercourse; and if it is not a [valid] levirate betrothal, it is the wife of the first [brother] with whom he has intercourse.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:13:3.hebrew: וחולץ לשניה - דחדא לא מיפטרא בביאה דאידך, דלמא מאמר לא קני והוו להו ב' יבמות הבאות מב' בתים. וייבומי תרווייהו נמי לא, דלמא מאמר קני והוו להו ב' יבמות הבאות מבית אחד:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:13:3.english: And he performs ḥalitza with the second - For one [of them] is not exempted by the intercourse with the other, [since] perhaps ma'amar [levirate betrothal] does not acquire, and [thus] they are two yevamot coming from two houses. And [performing] levirate marriage with both of them is also not [permitted], [since] perhaps ma'amar does acquire, and [thus] they are two yevamot coming from one house.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:14:1.english: If the levirate bond of two yevamim [is] by Torah [law], etc. - [The Gemara] raises [this] objection against the Rabbis.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:14:2.hebrew: אלא מדרבנן - דמדאורייתא מאמר לא קני, והוו להו שתי יבמות מב' בתים, ותרוייהו מצי לייבומי. ורבנן הוא דגזרו שמא יאמרו ב' יבמות הבאות מבית א' מתייבמות:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:14:2.english: Rather, [it is] by rabbinic [law] - For by Torah law, ma'amar [levirate betrothal] does not acquire [completely], and they are two yevamot from two households, so both of them may enter into levirate marriage. And it is the Rabbis who decreed [against it], lest [people] say two yevamot who come from one household may enter into levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:2:1.hebrew: תנא בקידושין - ספק קרוב לו כו', וה"ה בגירושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:2:1.english: [The Mishnah] taught regarding betrothal - [The case of] uncertainty [whether it landed] closer to him, etc., and the same applies to divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:2:2.hebrew: ותנא בגירושין - כתב בכתב ידו וכו', וה"ה לקידושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:2:2.english: And [the mishna] teaches with regard to divorce - [The case where] he wrote [the bill of divorce] in his own handwriting, etc., and the same is true with regard to betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: כל שיש בקידושין יש בגירושין, ויש בגירושין מה שאין בקידושין. וזהו דגירושין לאו דוקא, ומשום דתנא זהו בקידושין, תנא נמי זהו בגירושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: All that exists in betrothal exists in divorce, and there is in divorce that which does not exist in betrothal. And [the phrase] "This is" regarding divorce is not specific, and because [the Tanna] taught "This is" regarding betrothal, he also taught "This is" regarding divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:2.hebrew: כל שיש בקידושין - כגון ספק קרוב לו וכו', הוי נמי ספק בגירושין:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:2.english: All that exists with regard to betrothal - For example, [a case of] uncertainty [whether it is] closer to him, etc., is also [a case of] uncertainty with regard to divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:3.hebrew: ויש בגירושין - שאין ספק לענין קדושין, כגון זמן, כדמפרש לקמן, דבשטר קידושין — כגון המקדש בשטר — לא תקנו זמן:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:3.english: And there are [cases] in divorce - where there is no uncertainty regarding betrothal, such as [the] date, as [the Gemara] explains below; for in a document of betrothal — such as one who betroths with a document — they did not institute [writing] a date.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:4.hebrew: וזהו דגירושין לאו דוקא - דמשמעו זהו דהוי ספק בגירושין, אבל ספק קרוב לא הוי ספק לגירושין. ואיידי דתנא זהו בקידושין, דדוקא זהו, דקמ"ל זהו ספק קרוב הוא דשייך בקידושין, אבל ספק זמן לא שייך בהו:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:4:4.english: And "this is" with regard to divorce is not specific - For it implies [that] "this is" what constitutes an uncertainty in divorce, whereas an uncertainty of "closer [to him or her]" is not an uncertainty for divorce. And since [the Mishnah] taught "this is" with regard to betrothal — where "this is" is specific, as it teaches us [that] "this is" an uncertainty of "closer [to him or her]" that applies to betrothal, whereas an uncertainty of date does not apply to it.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:5:1.hebrew: הניחא למ"ד - בגיטין בפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף כו:): מפני מה תקנו חכמים זמן בגיטין? משום פירי, לידע מאימתי תגבה מבעלה פירות שאכל מנכסי מלוג שלה, דקסבר משעה שנתן עיניו בה לגרשה שוב אין לו לבעל פירות:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:5:1.english: This works out well according to the one who says - In Gittin, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 26b): Why did the Sages institute [writing] a date in bills of divorce? Due to the produce [of her property], to know from when she may collect from her husband [for] produce that he consumed from her *nikhsei melog* [property whose yield belongs to the husband], for he holds [that] from the moment he set his eyes upon her to divorce her, the husband no longer has [rights to] the produce.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:5:2.hebrew: ארוסה לית לה פירי - לפיכך לא תקנוהו בשטר קידושין, שאין הבעל אוכל פירות עד שתכנס לחופה, דכי תקון רבנן פירי לבעל משום פרקונה, ופרקונה לא קא מחייב בה אלא מכתובה ואילך, דתנאי כתובה הוא, דאם תשתבאי אפרקינך, בכתובות פ' נערה (כתובות דף נא.):
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:5:2.english: There are no profits from a betrothed woman - Therefore, they did not institute [writing the date] in a deed of betrothal, for the husband does not consume the profits [of her property] until she enters the bridal canopy, because when the Rabbis instituted [that] the profits [belong] to the husband, [it was] on account of her ransom, and he is not obligated for her ransom except from [the time of] the ketubah onward, for it is a stipulation of the ketubah: "If you are taken captive, I will ransom you," in Ketubot, chapter Na'arah (Ketubot 51a).

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:6:1.hebrew: משום בת אחותו - שמא יהא נשוי בת אחותו ותזנה תחתיו, ויראה עדים ממשמשין ובאין, ויחוס עליה ויגרשנה, ויאמר: "קודם זנות שאתם מעידים, כבר נתגרשה":
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:6:1.english: Due to the daughter of his sister - Lest he be married to the daughter of his sister and she commit adultery while married to him, and he sees witnesses approaching, and he has pity on her and divorces her, and says: "Prior to the licentious act [about] which you are testifying, she was already divorced."

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:6:2.hebrew: ליתקין זמן - נמי בשטר קדושין, שמא תזנה ויאמר קודם קידושין הוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:6:2.english: They should institute [the] date - also in a deed of betrothal, lest she commit adultery and he say [that] it was before the betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:8:1.english: But [what about] a slave - [This refers to] the sale of a slave.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:8:2.hebrew: ותקון רבנן זמן - בכל שטרי מכירה [של עבד כדי] לידע מאיזה זמן יאכל פירות, שזה קנה נכסי עבדו:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:8:2.english: And the Sages instituted [writing] a date - In all bills of sale [of a slave, in order] to know from what time [the buyer] consumes the produce, for this [buyer] has acquired the property of his slave.

Rashi on Yevamot 31b:9:1.hebrew: מחקה ליה - לזמן, ותאמר: קודם קידושין היה זנות זה:
Rashi on Yevamot 31b:9:1.english: She will erase it - [She will erase] the date, and she will say: "This act of licentiousness was before the betrothal."

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:10:1.hebrew: דחזו בכתבא ואתו ומסהדי כו' - קשה לר"י, דבהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף צח. ושם:) גבי השורף שטרותיו של חבירו פריך: "ואי דאיכא סהדי דידעי, ליכתבו ליה שטרא אחרינא"; ואמאי, הא אמר הכא ד"מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם"? ואר"י דה"נ, אם היו מעידים שכך ראו בשטר — שפיר הוו עבדי, דהרי הם כאילו מעידים "ראינו עדות שנתקבל בב"ד", דעדים החתומים על השטר נעשה כמי שנחקרה עדותן בב"ד. אבל חיישינן שמא לא יעידו שכך ראו בשטר, אלא שמא יעידו על המעשה עצמו כאילו הם זוכרים, והם אינן זוכרין אלא על פי הכתב. וכן הא דאמרינן בפ"ב דכתובות (דף כ.): "כותב אדם עדותו על השטר ומעיד עליה אפילו אחר כמה שנים, והוא שזוכרה מעצמו, אבל אין זוכרה מעצמו — לא" — התם נמי לא איירי במעיד שכך ראה כתוב, אלא במעיד על מעשה עצמו; ועוד, דהתם לא הוה שטר, אלא שכותב לזכרון דברים בעלמא, ולא שייך למימר "נעשה כמי שנחקרה עדותו בב"ד". ואר"י דשמע מר"ת, שנוהגין עכשיו ששולחין העדים עדותן בכתב ידם לב"ד, ולא קרינן ביה "מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם", כיון שהם זוכרין עדותן. והא דתניא במי שאחזו (גיטין דף עא.): "'ואם לא יגיד' — פרט לאלם שאין יכול לדבר", ופריך: "ואמאי? והרי יכול לדבר מתוך הכתב! שאני עדות, דרחמנא אמר: 'מפיהם ולא מפי כתבם'" — שאני אלם שאין ראוי להגיד, כדאמרינן (מנחות דף קו:): "כל שאין ראוי לבילה כו'". אבל אחר — מועיל כתב ידו כשזוכר העדות. ומיהו בפירוש חומש (דברים י״ט:ט״ו) פרש"י: "ע"פ שנים עדים" — פרט שלא ישלחו כתבם לב"ד:
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:10:1.english: "When they see [the date] that is written and come forth to testify, etc." - This is difficult for R"I [Rabbeinu Yitzchak], for in [the chapter] HaGozel Kamma (Bava Kamma 98a and 98b), regarding one who burns his fellow's legal documents, [the Gemara] asks: "And if there are witnesses who know [the contents], let them write him another document!" And why [could they do so]? Surely [the Gemara] said here that [testimony must be] "from their mouths, and not from their writings"! And R"I answers that here too, if they were testifying that "so we saw [written] in a document," they would be acting properly, for they are as if testifying "we saw testimony that was accepted in court," since witnesses signed on a document are treated as if their testimony has already been examined in court. However, we are concerned lest they not testify that "so we saw in a document," but rather lest they testify about the incident itself as if they remember [it], when [in fact] they only remember it based on the writing. And similarly, that which we say in the second chapter of Ketubot (20a): "A person may write his testimony on a document and testify about it even after several years, provided that he remembers it on his own, but if he does not remember it on his own — no" — there too, it is not dealing with one who testifies that "so I saw written," but rather with one who testifies about the incident itself. Furthermore, there it was not a [formal] legal document, rather he writes [it] merely as a memorandum, and it is not applicable to say "it is treated as if his testimony was examined in court." And R"I said that he heard from R"T [Rabbeinu Tam] that nowadays the practice is that witnesses send their testimony in their own handwriting to the court, and we do not apply to it "from their mouths, and not from their writings," since they remember their testimony. And as for that which is taught in [a baraita in the chapter] Mi SheAchazo (Gittin 71a): "'And if he does not tell' — this excludes a mute person who cannot speak," and [the Gemara] asks: "Why [is he excluded]? Surely he can speak via writing! [Rather,] testimony is different, for the Merciful One said: 'From their mouths, and not from their writings'" — a mute person is different, because he is not fit to tell [orally], as we say (Menachot 106b): "Anything that is not fit for mingling, etc." However, for another [person who can speak], his handwriting is effective when he remembers the testimony. Nevertheless, in [his] commentary on the Chumash (Deuteronomy 19:15), Rashi explained: "'By the mouth of two witnesses' — this excludes [a case where] they send their writing to the court."

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:11:1.hebrew: להצלה דידה קאתי - פי' בקונט' דהשתא דתיקון זמן, אי לא מייתא שטרא דאיגרשה מקמי הכי, מוקמינן לה אחזקת אשת איש וקטלינן לה. ואין נראה, דבהדיא אמר בפ' שני דגיטין (דף יז:): "גזייה לזמן ויהביה ניהלה, מה הועילו חכמים בתקנתן?", ומשני: "לרמאי לא חיישינן". אלמא כי ליכא זמן לא קטלינן לה. ואר"י דה"פ: "להצלה דידה קאתי" — שהגט בא להצילה ולהגיד שהיא מגורשת, ולכך יראה למחוק הזמן, כי סבורה שיפסול בכך וגרע כחו טפי; אבל ודאי אי הוה מחקת ליה, לא הוה קטלינן לה. "הכא לחובה דידה קאתי" — דהקידושין באין להעיד שהיא מקודשת, ומחקה ליה לעולם לזמן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:11:1.english: "It comes to save her" - Rashi explains that now that they enacted [writing] a date, if she does not bring a document [proving] that she was divorced prior to that [time], we establish her under the presumption of being a married woman and execute her. But this does not seem [correct], for [the Gemara] explicitly states in the second chapter of Gittin (17b): "[If] he cut off the date and gave it to her, what have the Sages accomplished with their enactment?" And it answers: "We are not concerned about a deceiver." Thus, when there is no date, we do not execute her. Rather, Rabbi Yitzchak says that this is its explanation: "It comes to save her" — for the bill of divorce comes to save her and to declare that she is divorced, and therefore she is afraid to erase the date, because she thinks that it will thereby be disqualified and its legal force is weakened; however, certainly if she had erased it, we would not execute her. "Here, it comes to her disadvantage" — for the betrothal [deed] comes to testify that she is betrothed, and she would always erase the date.

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:12:1.hebrew: שלשה אחין נשואין ג' נשים נכריות - הו"מ למנקט "ואחד מופנה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:12:1.english: Three brothers married to three unrelated women - It could have stated "and one [of them] is unmarried."

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:14:1.hebrew: מדרבנן וגזירה כו' - משמע דאשת ב' מתים בשום מקום לא הויא אלא מדרבנן, דאי לאו גזירה דהכא היתה מתייבמת אפי' בעלת מאמר, ולא גזרינן לה אטו אשת שני מתים; וא"כ, "מי שעליה זיקת יבם אחד כו'" לא הויא דרשא גמורה, אלא אסמכתא בעלמא. וקשה, דבפרק בתרא דגיטין (דף פב: ושם) אמרי': "אלא אשת ב' מתים היכי משכחת לה?", משמע דהוי דאורייתא ואפי' בחד דוכתא! וי"ל דפלוגתא דתנאי היא, כדמוכח לקמן בסוף האשה רבה (יבמות דף צו:) גבי בן תשע שבא על יבמתו ומשהגדיל נשא אשה אחרת ומת, השניה חולצת או מתייבמת, הראשונה שהיא בעלת זיקת שני יבמין חולצת ולא מתייבמת. ופריך בגמרא: "ויעשו ביאת בן תשע כמאמר בגדול, ותדחה צרה מיבום?" — פירוש: כי הכא. ומסיק לרבי יוחנן דעשו ועשו, ופליג תנא דשמעתין אההוא תנא; דהאי תנא דשמעתין גזר משום צרה — פירוש: הא דקא אסר בעלת מאמר, משום דאיכא צרה בהדה, כדגזר בשמעתין דלמא חליץ והדר מייבם, כדפירש בקונטרס, אבל משום זיקת שני יבמין לא מיתסרא דלאו דאורייתא, ומיהו כי ליכא צרה בהדה נמי אסורה אטו היכא דאיכא צרה, כדקאמר התם רבא לעיל דאפי' היכא דליכא צרה בהדה מיחלץ חלצה, יבומי לא מייבמא. ותנא דהתם לא גזר משום צרה — פי': הא דקא אסר לבעלת ביאת בן תשע לייבומי, לאו משום צרה, אלא אטו אשת שני מתים דהוי בעלמא דאורייתא, ודוקא בדידה גזרו אבל בצרתה לא, דלא רצו להחמיר גם בצרתה אטו אשת שני מתים — וההיא דריש המגרש (גיטין פב:) כההוא תנא. וריב"ן פירש שם דלכולי עלמא אשת שני מתים דאורייתא, ותנא דהכא גזר אף באשת השני משום צרה, דהיינו בעלת מאמר, דקא סבר כיון דבעלמא אשת שני מתים דאורייתא מחמירי אפי' באידך, ותנא דהתם לא מחמיר כולי האי ולא גזר באשתו של בן תשע אטו בעלת זיקת שני יבמים. וקשה, דהכא מסיק דטעמא דהך תנא משום הנך גזירות דמפרש הכא; ועוד, דהתם קרי רבא לאשתו צרה, וקאמר נמי "ויעשו ביאת בן תשע כמאמר בגדול ותדחה צרה כו'", והכא קרי לבעלת מאמר צרה. וריב"ן הקשה לעצמו שתי קושיות הללו, ופר"י עיקר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:14:1.english: "By rabbinic [law], and [it is a] decree, etc." - This implies that [the prohibition against] the wife of two deceased [brothers] is nowhere [applicable] except by rabbinic [law]; for were it not for the decree here, even the woman who received ma'amar [levirate betrothal] would enter into levirate marriage, and we would not enact a decree regarding her on account of [the prohibition of] the wife of two deceased [brothers]. And if so, [the exposition of] "she upon whom rests the levirate bond of one yavam, etc." is not a full-fledged [biblical] exposition, but merely a scriptural support [for a rabbinic law]. And this is difficult, for in the last chapter of Gittin (82b and thereabouts) [the Gemara] says: "Rather, how can [the case of] the wife of two deceased [brothers] be found?", which implies that it is by Torah [law], even in one place! And one can answer that it is a dispute among Tannaim, as is proven later at the end of [chapter] Ha'isha Rabbah (Yevamot 96b), regarding a nine-year-old boy who cohabited with his yevamah, and after he came of age he married another woman and died: the second [wife] performs ḥalitzah or enters into levirate marriage, [while] the first [wife], who is subject to the levirate bond of two yevamin, performs ḥalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage. And the Gemara asks: "Let them treat the cohabitation of a nine-year-old like ma'amar by an adult, so that the rival wife should be rejected from levirate marriage?" — meaning, like here. And [the Gemara] concludes according to Rabbi Yoḥanan that they treated [the nine-year-old's cohabitation like ma'amar] and [also] treated [it like full marriage], and the Tanna of our passage disagrees with that Tanna. For this Tanna of our passage decreed [the prohibition] on account of the rival wife — meaning, that he prohibits the woman who received ma'amar because there is a rival wife with her, as [the Gemara] decrees in our passage lest he perform ḥalitzah [with one] and then enter into levirate marriage [with the other], as Rashi explained; however, on account of the levirate bond of two yevamin she is not prohibited, because it is not by Torah [law] — yet even when there is no rival wife with her she is also prohibited, on account of [the case] where there is a rival wife, as Rava states there earlier that even where there is no rival wife with her she performs ḥalitzah [and] does not enter into levirate marriage. Whereas the Tanna there did not decree on account of the rival wife — meaning, that he prohibits the woman with whom the nine-year-old cohabited from entering into levirate marriage not on account of the rival wife, but rather on account of [the prohibition of] the wife of two deceased [brothers], which is generally by Torah [law]; and they decreed specifically regarding her, but not regarding her rival wife, because they did not wish to be stringent with her rival wife as well on account of [the prohibition of] the wife of two deceased [brothers] — and that [passage] at the beginning of [chapter] Hamegaresh (Gittin 82b) follows that Tanna. And Rivan [Rabbi Yehudah ben Natan] explained there that according to everyone, [the prohibition of] the wife of two deceased [brothers] is by Torah [law]; and the Tanna here decreed even regarding the wife of the second [brother] on account of the rival wife — that is, the woman who received ma'amar — because he holds that since generally [the prohibition of] the wife of two deceased [brothers] is by Torah [law], we are stringent even regarding the other [woman], whereas the Tanna there is not so stringent and did not decree regarding the [adult] wife of the nine-year-old on account of the woman subject to the levirate bond of two yevamin. And this is difficult, for here [the Gemara] concludes that the reason of this Tanna is on account of these decrees that it explains here! Furthermore, there Rava calls his [adult] wife "the rival wife" and also says, "Let them treat the cohabitation of a nine-year-old like ma'amar by an adult, so that the rival wife should be rejected, etc.", whereas here he calls the woman who received ma'amar "the rival wife"! And Rivan raised both of these difficulties for himself, and the explanation of R"I [Rabbeinu Yitzḥak] is the primary one.

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:1:1.hebrew: וארעא אוקמא בחזקת בר שטיא - לא דמי לההיא דאמר בקידושין (דף עט:) ובבבא בתרא (דף קנג: ושם): "אם בריא הוא, עליו להביא ראיה ששכיב מרע היה, ואם שכיב מרע הוא כו'"; דהכא, כיון שדרכו להיות עתים חלים ועתים שוטה, לא שייך להעמידו אחזקה כמו שהוא עתה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:1:1.english: And let the land remain in the possession of Bar Shatya - [This] is not similar to that which [the Gemara] says in Kiddushin (79b) and in Bava Batra (153b and there): "If he is healthy [now], it is upon him to bring proof that he was on his deathbed, and if he is on his deathbed [now], etc."; for here, since it is his way to be at times sane and at times insane, it is not applicable to establish him on a presumptive status as he is now.

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:3:1.hebrew: אי יגיד עליו ריעו מאי זו היא דקתני - הוה מצי למיפרך: אי "יגיד עליו ריעו", ליתני כולהו בחד, וליתני חד מינייהו באידך, כדפריך בפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף יט.):
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:3:1.english: If "his fellow speaks of him," what is "this is" that it teaches - [The Gemara] could have asked: If "his fellow speaks of him," let [the Mishnah] teach all of them in one [place], and let it teach [just] one of them in the other [place], as [the Gemara] asks in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 19a).

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:4:1.hebrew: למעוטי זמן דליתיה בקידושין - מספקא לר"י: כתב בכתב ידו ואין עליו עדים, אי מהני בקידושין אי לא; דכיון שאין צריך זמן, מה לנו אם אין עליו עדים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:4:1.english: To exclude the date, which is not [applicable] in betrothal - Ri is uncertain: [if] one wrote [a betrothal document] in his own handwriting and there are no witnesses on it, whether it is effective for betrothal or not; for since a date is not required, what does it matter to us if there are no witnesses on it?

Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:8:1.hebrew: והא עבדא דאיכא דקני בכספא כו' - פירש בקונטרס שטר קניית עבד. וקשה לר"י: דא"כ, מ"ש דנקט עבד, דהו"מ למינקט שטר מכירת קרקע וכל שטרי מקח וממכר? ועוד, דהתם לא תיקון רבנן זמן. ונראה דאשטר שיחרור קאי, דתיקון זמן לידע מתי נאסר בשפחה והותר בבת ישראל. וה"ק: "והא עבדא איכא דקני נפשיה בכספא ואיכא דקני בשטרא". והשתא ניחא הא דמשני: "התם רובא וכו'". וא"ת: בפ"ק דגיטין (דף ט.) דתנן "בג' דרכים שוו גיטי נשים לשחרורי עבדים", ליתני נמי זמן, ששוו גיטי נשים לשחרורי עבדים וליתיה בקידושין? וי"ל: דכל מילי דחשיב התם ודפריך התם הוי חד טעמא בגיטי נשים ושחרורי עבדים, אבל זמן דשחרורי עבדים בא להתירו בבת ישראל, וגיטי נשים משום פירי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 31b:8:1.english: "But [with regard to] a slave, where there are [those] who acquire with money," etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained [that the Gemara refers to] a deed of purchase of a slave. And this is difficult for the Ri: For if so, why did [the Gemara] specifically mention a slave, when it could have mentioned a deed of sale of land or any deeds of buying and selling? Furthermore, there [in those cases], the Sages did not institute [writing] a date. And it appears that [the Gemara] refers to a bill of emancipation, where they instituted [writing] a date to know when he became forbidden to a maidservant and permitted to a Jewish woman. And this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "But [with regard to] a slave, there are [those] who acquire themselves with money and there are [those] who acquire [themselves] with a deed." And now, that which [Rav Ashi] answers — "There, the majority," etc. — is well understood. And if you ask: In the first chapter of Gittin (9a), where we learned in a Mishnah: "In three ways, bills of divorce of women are equal to [bills of] emancipation of slaves," let [the Mishnah] also teach [the requirement of] a date, since [in that respect] bills of divorce of women are equal to [bills of] emancipation of slaves, and it does not apply to betrothal? And one can answer: All the matters that [the Mishnah] enumerates there, and those that [the Gemara] raises as objections there, have one [and the same] reason in bills of divorce of women and [bills of] emancipation of slaves; whereas the date of [bills of] emancipation of slaves comes to permit him to a Jewish woman, while [in] bills of divorce of women [it is] because of produce [i.e., the usufruct of the wife's property].
